I think this feature should be either removed or changed to do not check for the following reasons:

  1. When Microsoft moves to the upcoming cumulative update release method, users will no longer be able to choose individual updates to install/uninstall. Therefore, Ancile users will have no use for Windows Update.

  2. Users that have Windows Update set to do not check must remember to change it back after running Ancile.

  3. By setting check/notify, Microsoft is able actively monitor how many machines are avoiding updates and which updates are not being installed. I don't think they should be privy to this information; the evidence of Microsoft's underhandedness is overwhelming.

If this feature is modified to set do not check, I recommend Ancile also stop and disable the Windows Update service.

These are all very good points and I may implement them in the future

  1. Microsoft's new update strategy is a bit concerning, and the end result may be to stop accepting updates. However, until they do switch over and we have a better understanding of what we're up against, I think it's better to be able to keep Windows update running. The next step would be simply blocking and hiding each update that comes out (Until we can't do that anymore). If we're lucky, someone will figure out a way to get rid of the parts of updates we don't want so that we can install necessary updates without all the junk.
  2. That actually didn't cross my mind while I was working on this. It's an excellent point. I'll have to look into checking to see if this is enabled before I just overwrite someone's settings.
  3. I don't like the idea of Microsoft monitoring my update status either. I may change to "do not check" in the future. Right now I'm trying to maintain a balance, and give updates the benefit of the doubt, but that's getting more difficult over time.

Overall, the idea behind stopping Windows update from automatically installing was to give users time to figure out if they wanted to install the updates, and to allow me time to add blocked updates and push out a new version of Ancile. The hope was that the new round of updates would be benign and could be installed without issue. Unfortunately, this is becoming more difficult.

For the time being, I'm going to keep this functionality mostly unchanged until it's inevitable that Windows updates need to be completely disabled.

Thanks for your input. This is just the kind of feedback I was looking for.

Thanks for the detailed reply.

I don't like the idea of Microsoft monitoring my update status either

Actually, my concern wasn't Microsoft's knowledge of my update status or which updates I had installed. Rather, it was that check/notify allows Microsoft to be aware of thousands of machines missing the same updates (those blocked my Ancile). With the knowledge of this pattern, it would not surprise me if they came up with yet another nefarious method to force update on users. In other words, we should give them as little information as possible so as to not tempt fate.
